question:
Which of the following is equivalent to

\[\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{1-\dfrac{x-1}{x}}}\]

when \(x \lt 0?\)
solution:
First simplify the denominator inside the radical. Since \(x<0\), we have \(x\ne0\), so
\[
1-\frac{x-1}{x}
=\frac{x-(x-1)}{x}
=\frac1x.
\]
This denominator is also nonzero. Hence the radicand becomes
\[
\frac{x}{1/x}=x^2>0.
\]
The square-root symbol denotes the nonnegative square root, so
\[
\sqrt{x^2}=|x|=-x
\]
because \(x<0\). Therefore the expression is \(\boxed{-x}\), choice A.
